conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Mixing Console
style.description: A vintage analogue recording console shot close and low across its surface in warm studio light: brushed-aluminium channel strips between walnut end-cheeks, long-throw faders, coloured rotary knobs with pointer lines, lit square push-buttons, LED bargraphs, a meter bridge of needle VU meters with warm backlit cream faces, white console tape with hand-written channel names, a jog wheel, and tape reels turning behind in shallow focus. Settings made physical: every control is a labelled parameter — faders glide to planned values (grouped, as if automated), knobs click through detents, buttons latch and light — and the meters respond with real needle ballistics to each channel's level x fader; a master meter sums the mix, solo and mute change it, an EQ knob reshapes a curve display. The sound is the mix: each channel is a synthesized layer whose loudness follows its fader.
motion: Faders glide to planned values as automation: a group of faders starts, moves and lands together, with a tiny motorised settle.
Knobs turn through detents (dwell, snap, tick); buttons press down, latch and light (mute amber, solo green).
Meters respond: each VU needle and LED column is the closed-form 2nd-order response to its channel's planned notes x fader; the master meter sums the channels.
Solo one channel and every other meter falls; mute one and the master reading drops — the sound follows exactly.
EQ beat: a HI/MID knob turns and the curve display reshapes on the meter bridge.
Camera: low and close across the surface, sliding along the strips to whatever is being adjusted; a wide at the end.

objects.procedural: slatted walnut studio wall 2.7 m behind the console + dark floor
reel-to-reel tape machine behind the console: walnut cabinet, brushed faceplate, two turning aluminium reels, head block

notes.data: SAMPLE DATA: channel levels, fader positions and meter readings are placeholders (stamped on screen).
notes.mechanism: mixplan.js: automation tracks -> fader/knob/button positions; a 120 bpm four-bar pattern -> notes; each note's gain = velocity x level x fader law x EQ x mute/solo x master at its onset; meters = closed-form 2nd-order needle response to those notes; SCORE = the same notes synthesized.
notes.framing: window check ok (worst over -0.0128 at 15s); kit 90% safe ok (worst 0.8872)
